chapters.html:
Phainon had always known that coming from a famous family of solely heralded vampire hunters, his best friend in the entire world shouldn’t be one of those very things they sought to exterminate indiscriminately.

That would be completely silly and foolish of him to do, yet as he laid there in the field of wheat he and his best friend always met at, feeling those pointed and sharpened canines sinking deeper into his neck to pierce the blood from his body - he still didn’t really mind knowing Mydei is a vampire.

That was fine!

Even as he blinked at the sky above them, staring at the rising night sky that seemed to stretch forever that was slightly blocked by blonde hair feasting on him.

He didn’t mind this at all.

If anything, he felt his own hands move to cradle around his childhood friend - gently brushing through his hair as he swallowed up Phainon’s blood, guzzling it down at almost an alarming rate.

Maybe a rate so fast Phainon would have cared about if it were anyone but Mydeimos.

“You must have been really hungry to attack me like this, huh..?” Phainon murmured to him as he slowly petted his head soothingly, not even sure if Mydei was paying him any mind right now.

Probably not.

For Mydei to have lunged at him to chomp down on him so hungrily..  He didn’t think anything like that would ever happen. Mydei had always shown such discipline with regards to Phainon’s blood..

Sure, Phainon had noticed the pointed fangs and how he didn’t seem very fond of the sun and almost tried to hide from it when Phainon dragged him into it - but Phainon was in denial. 

Probably because he always had wanted to keep Mydeimos to himself and safe.

He knew.. Of course he knew.. 

He knew that if anyone ever found out about his friend, they would hurt him, or do even worse. Those thoughts alone made Phainon’s hands tighten on Mydei’s head, tenderly pressing him down more against his neck as he seemed to suck Phainon’s life away.

That was fine.

Phainon would forgive him if he died under Mydei today, at least then he would have truly been useful to the vampire. That’s all he had grown to want anyway as his fingers continued combing through those locks of hair - gently massaging Mydei to soothe him as he ate his fill. 

It hurt.

It wasn't a comfortable or nice feeling to have Mydei drinking him alive, it was a dull aching pain stabbing away in his neck - one that only seemed to get worse with every brutal suck Mydei gave onto his neck.

But it was Mydei doing that to him, and he had long since known he could never deny Mydei from things he wanted - even if he tried to tease about it and act like it was a competition. He always had Mydei in the forefront of his mind. 

He had long since known he loved Mydei more than he could ever possibly love himself.

But that bite didn’t last forever, as Mydei finished drinking his fill he eventually broke away - quickly jerking backwards from Phainon and out of his hands with harshened movements. 

“I.. Shouldn’t have done that..” Mydei’s voice was quiet - almost as if he was holding back a pathetic sob from escaping his throat that was mixed with pure horror and dread.

But Phainon couldn’t understand that as he watched Mydei scramble a few feet away, only making Phainon rise slowly into a sitting position to blink at him in slight wonder. Those wide golden cat-like eyes always seemed to be on the hunt - hungry beneath the surface when they looked at Phainon.

But Phainon had come to terms with that side of Mydei so long ago - the bite was nothing he didn’t already expect to happen eventually when he really thought about it. Even if Phainon had assumed it would have been him willingly letting Mydei bite him.. 

Not the powerful lunge Mydei had given him today to force him to the floor and clawed hands gripping at him to make him stay down. As if Phainon was going to fight against Mydei.

Phainon felt a small laugh flutter out of his lips, grinning at Mydei from his spot on the ground before moving to rub at that tender and bruised skin on his neck; “It’s okay! You were probably just really hungry, right?”

“You..” Mydei trailed off, still appearing so very wide eyed and terrified that Phainon found himself swiftly dropping his hand from his neck and instead moving to adjust his shirt - fixing it to cover up that spot where Mydei’s fangs had just been. 

“It’s okay, don’t worry! I’ll hide the bite, see?” Phainon told him before giving a lop-sided smile, hoping that he could reassure his best friend and only friend.

That he could comfort and console his worries away just like normal..

“No..” Mydei muttered out as he slowly shook his head side to side, as if he didn’t want to listen with such a childish reaction, and well. He was a few years younger than Phainon, anyway. 

“Really, Mydei.. It’s okay..” Phainon tried to softly tell him, tried to coax Mydei into believing his  best friend’s words.

Because for Mydei.. He would lie about everything if he had to.

Mydei.. This vampire.. Was the only person that had ever treated Phainon like an actual person, more than some vampire hunting tool, born and bred solely to fight creatures of the night. Trained day in and day out to hate them, only to have the only gentle and beloved thing in his life be one of those very creatures.

It was ironic..

Mydei only shook his head more at that, harshly and swiftly, appearing more and more upset the more he slowly stepped away from Phainon, “Forget.. You ever knew me.”

“M.. Mydei, what do you mean? It’s okay, no one will find out about the bite or about you!” Phainon once more reassured him as he forced himself to his feet, only gritting his teeth as Mydei seemed to dart away at that. Running away..

Away from Phainon.. 

“Mydei-” 

Phainon stumbled.

A stumble that would haunt him for ages, one that he took a moment to recover from as his vision seemed painfully dizzy and blurred - probably due to his loss of blood as he struggled to balance on his own feet before throwing his head upwards. Eyes staring after that still quickly scurrying away Mydei through the wheat, all he could do was try to move after him.

But it was so heavy on his heart already.

The picture of Mydei appearing so worried, so terrified while looking at him - he had never done that before. Never once had he looked at Phainon like that. He was always happy and smiling, even during their silly wrestling competitions, he was always Phainon’s own personal sunshine. 

“Mydei, wait! Don’t go!” Phainon called after him again, forcing his feet to move after the fellow teen - only it was too late.

He knew that as he stopped at the edge of the forest and stared into it.

He knew that as his eyes no longer could spot the fiery golden haired boy and didn’t know where to go to even follow after him.

He knew that as he felt himself tearing up over the way his best friend had so swiftly became afraid of him.

And then Phainon waited.

Every single day after his training, every single night.

He sat in their wheat field for Mydei to come back - for Mydei to come play with him again, for Mydei to grin at him and take part in their stupid competitions again.

And he never did.

Not even as the days turned to months, and months into years - Phainon waited for that vampire to come back to him. 

Just..

Phainon never saw Mydei again, he could only look at the spot where Mydei had disappeared into the forest that day, and regret more and more that he didn’t try more to chase him down.

‘Vampire hunter’.

That was an ironic line of family heritage for Phainon to be from, even as he finally graduated and was allowed to go out into the work field, away from home, further away from their special meeting spot. 

It felt ironic.

After all, the only vampire he was actively hunting - he had no desire of actually harming.

He just wanted his Mydeimos back.

That meant doing anything for that cause and goal, anyway.

That’s what he had to tell himself every single time as he took the life of another fellow vampire hunter again, blood dripping from his sword that was supposed to kill those ‘foul’ beasts. Staring at the lifeless eyes of another human as he stood in the doorway, mesmerized by the blood slowly seeping from their wounds. 

No one ever expected him to show up to their bounties and kill them, why would they?

They were all raised, bred, and taught to kill vampires, not their fellow vampire hunters, raised to trust each other to have their backs. Taught that this was their one and true purpose in this world - that their hands were made only for this duty to aid the public..

But there was only one person in this world who he actually wanted to protect, one person that had carved their spot into his heart leisurely and agonizingly. A hole in his heart that only they could fill, and then promptly ran away in fear of him when Mydei had finally yet accidentally laid himself out bare. 

This was the only answer. 

He couldn’t let some other vampire hunter find Mydei before him first and actually risk hurting him. Phainon had to find Mydei first, and keep him nice and safe away from the world - no matter the cost and the amount of blood shed for it.

That was always what he told himself as he slowly crouched to clean the human blood off his sword leisurely with a handkerchief - eyes still watching the blood flow from his deceased comrade from behind his mask. 

The vampire they were out hunting didn’t turn out to be Mydei - but that’s fine.

Phainon didn’t dare let them live til their next hunt either, how could he?

“The sun is annoying today..” Mydei had once grumbled as Phainon tugged him along, and Phainon could only laugh over that reaction from his best and dearest friend.

Mydei always hated being in the sun - even if Phainon tried putting his coat over him to block it more politely. Mydei still would scowl and fume over it all, it was one of the few things that seemed to truly anger and annoy Mydei that Phainon had found. 

Phainon hummed after his brief laughter, tightening his hand holding Mydei’s as he tugged him to their usual spot; “Hmm? It’s not even that bright out today! It’s overcast, Mydeimos!” 

“But..” Mydei’s small whine trailed off - making an odd sniffling noise as he followed Phainon regardless, and Phainon at that tossed a look over his shoulder to the slower, slacking off Mydeimos.

“C’mon! We can sit in the shade and just talk today.” Phainon offered, knowing fully well Mydei was sluggish on sunny days, he still showed up to play with Phainon - but he always seemed sleepy or just flat out exhausted in the sunlight. 

Phainon knew why, of course he did, how could he not as a child raised by vampire hunters? 

But that didn’t stop him from giving soft smiles to the boy that had never once harmed him, and even if he did one day, Phainon wouldn’t mind! Being best friends meant he would forgive Mydei for his mistakes and comfort him!

The idea of punishing Mydei for his own uncontrollable nature and hunger made Phainon feel nauseous to even consider it..

“Okay..” Mydei mumbled his reply, feet slowly following after the human tugging him along until they reached their destination. 

Phainon didn’t even hesitate as he sat down and yanked Mydei downwards with him - forcing the fellow teen to sit in the shade with him. 

It was a good waste of time.. To just relax and sit under the tree, watching the fields of wheat blow back and forth in the cool breeze..

Phainon didn’t even know how long he sat there with Mydei’s hand in his own before the vampire decided to speak. 

“I’ll marry you one day, I think..”

Phainon felt himself stiffen at those words, only to give a light-hearted laugh at those words, tilting his head to blink at the smaller boy next to him; “Marry me? But we’re both boys!”

Mydei blinked at him, at his words, taking a moment to seemingly think about Phainon’s reply before knitting his own brows together; “Oh.. So you don’t want to marry me when we’re older?”

“Nope!” Phainon instantly told him with a bark of laughter, letting go of Mydei’s hand to instead hug his own knees as he pulled them up to his chest.

Marrying another boy sounded so silly.

“Oh.. Okay, sorry..”

Those memories were always humorous and almost painful to recall.

They were so young back then, and it was the only time Mydei had ever said such things like that to him - even as the years passed and went by and Phainon found himself longing to hear them again up until the very moment those fangs sank into his skin.

And even past that moment - he would have said yes so long as Mydeimos had come back into his life..

Marry him.

Mydei had once wanted to marry him in the future, and Phainon in his youth had immediately told him no.

Ironic, considering now the only person and option that actually existed in Phainon’s love life was Mydei. The only person he had ever wanted to hold was Mydei, and the only person that had stolen his heart and then left his life forever was also Mydei.

Ironic.

Would it have been different if Phainon had been happy and accepted before Mydei bit him?

If Phainon had said yes as a child and promised himself to Mydei like that young bright child wanted instead of denying his cute little crush on Phainon?

Would Mydei have trusted him more when he bit into his skin to not run away after it?

Would he have felt safer knowing Phainon had already promised to love him?

Phainon didn’t know.

He was a few years older than his Mydeimos.. And in their youth, Mydei was just a smiley happy little guy. So painfully innocent towards his own existence as a vampire, and so attached to a human that he wanted to marry him.. And Phainon had told him no.

Phainon pressed out a deep and heavy sigh over those memories always resurfacing as he forced himself to straighten out - stretching lazily with a yawn as he put his sword away into its hilt once more.

Eyes only dancing to study the mangled corpse, making sure it assuredly would not be getting back up - before rolling his shoulders and closing the old wooden door behind him as the blood drenched the floor. 

Phainon had done this so many times that his hands no longer even shook as he backstabbed people, as he cut and diced them into pieces, all he had to do to calm himself was think about that man.

Mydeimos.

How had he grown up to be?

Was he still the same man that wanted to marry Phainon?

Because Phainon certainly would take him up on that offer now, he would even write their vows in blood if it meant his hands at least got to cradle Mydei’s head so gently between his fingers once he was done taking whoever lives Mydei wanted.

To be honest, as Phainon walked through the icy air of the night and through town - he always found himself jealous when thinking about Mydei.

How many humans had Mydei bitten that weren’t him?

How many had he stooped down to licking and slurping away at to sate his own hunger desperately..?

Phainon wanted to do that for him - to feed him everyday of his life and completely remove the struggle. He wanted those lips on himself only, and that desire only got worse and worse as the years went by. 

It had to.

He had to fully accept his delusions lest he even consider the fact Mydeimos may already be dead through other vampire hunters. Lest he consider the idea that Mydei hadn’t even gotten to grow up at all - that someone had cut his life short and Phainon would never know about it.

It drove him even more insane than the hours he spent searching for any information on the vampire. Even considering it made his chest ache dully, numbly hearing the thudding of his own heart in his ears with every numb step back to the vampire hunter tavern and outpost, every numb step remained so very heavy and hard to take as he walked.

Phainon Khaslana.. One of the famed vampire hunter families, someone no one ever batted an eye at, someone no one ever even considered he was the rampant murderer hunting down fellow vampire hunters.

But he had to.

If he stopped for even a moment, if he slowed in this direction of his life, he feared there would be no humanity even left to look back at him in the mirrors of his life. This path he had chosen was one not meant for someone that desired such a thing, anyway.

He had long since given up those human ideals for the much more interesting prospect of having the only person he had ever loved by his side - and sacrificing his own humanity was a small cost to pay when that man he desired wasn’t even human himself.

If he had to become a monster to fit in with a man the world saw as a monster, he would gladly do just that. 

His feelings on that matter would never change, not even as he removed his mask leisurely and slid his hood down - sighing before swiping his card to return into the rundown appearing vampire hunter tavern. Shabby, worn down, and nothing anyone would expect houses so many murderers. 

“Have you heard about what the higher ups are saying?”

Phainon barely batted an eye at those words that were quietly said at a round table to his side when he stepped inside - the higher ups were nothing he paid any mind to anyway.

They never paid any mind to his existence either, everyone merely assumed he was doing his work just like the rest of his family. Wholly unaware of his daily ritual of taking so many lives with his own hands just to protect a vampire..

“Yeah.. Kind of makes sense why they’re not pushing out many bounties right now..”

Well.

That was strange, Phainon was quite a busy person with his whole ‘hunting down vampire(s) while also hunting down humans’ routine he had adapted. He didn’t even know they were refusing to give out many bounties lately. 

“All the royal vampiric bloodlines are supposed to be in town.. That’s crazy spooky isn’t it?”

Phainon froze at that - just for a mere moment before moving to the bar leisurely, close enough to continue overhearing conversations and order something to quench his thirst. (Apple juice.)

“They’re all super powerful compared to normal vampires..”

“Best to stay clear of the area for the next few days..”

Phainon couldn’t stay clear, how could he?

There were so many royal vampiric bloodlines he had never seen before - so many new possibilities to find and chase down his Mydeimos. He couldn’t stay clear.

Finding that vampire was his lifelong dream, and if he had to suffer or die to get there - so be it. He didn’t mind how many souls he had to cleave down by his sword, or whose feet he had to step on. He had long since lost his own touch with reality while trying to even find that vampire that had bitten him and this disappeared..

Going into a horde of vampires ready to feast on any vampire hunter they saw? It was worth it, so long as he found any trace of Mydei, even the faintest trail of him. 

He had to.. He had to find him eventually.. Not finding him wasn’t even a possibility anymore. 

Everything after those words felt like a blur, a mess of eavesdropping on people, a mess of reading online on his phone, and a complete catastrophe of scrolling threads made by people deemed insane by those unaware vampires truly exist.

It truly was practically a giant vampire council meeting of all the master vampire families gathering - for what? 

Phainon didn’t know, he didn’t care either.

But there were names of families he didn’t know here, names of vampires he had no idea about. 

Not Mydeimos, however, and Phainon had no idea what his last name even was - so the threads listing out the vampire families felt like a mess of letters that made no sense to him.

It didn’t matter, he had to go there either way, even if it was simply to lurk and watch from afar. He had to go there and try to figure it all out. 

In a few days, at least, apparently it hadn’t started yet according to the mess of sources telling people to stay out of town. 

And Phainon could only mourn the fact that it hadn’t as he threw his phone to the side of his bed lazily.

The next few days passed in a messy blur, probably due to his ever decaying mental state, everyday was the same for him. It always had been since Mydei had left, as if time had truly stopped for him without the other half of himself to complete him.

This one, this one job was different, however as he followed behind this woman.

A mass of vampires..

Young vampires.

They were being kept and protected at this location, a shabby house that looked like nothing from the inside just like usual. 

Being kept safe with love and care with other grown vampires, apparently, but now were simply cattle waiting to be slaughtered by this woman vampire hunter as she moves through the night. As she walked her last night alive. 

This was slightly personal, anyway.

Considering the ages of these children, he couldn’t help but painfully remember the way Mydei may have died as well at their age. Maybe even to this very same woman as he leisurely followed behind her at every turn. 

It wasn’t fair.

To kill them when they were so young, they did nothing wrong by being born vampires - no one controls the circumstances they are born into. It infuriated Phainon to no end, even as he followed her through the door into the house silently, he couldn’t bite down his own rage.

Children.

They were just children in here.

And every step he took after her, he knew they would be just as terrified of him as they were of her. He was no different than her in their eyes, just like he hadn’t been in Mydeimos’s. Vampiric children are taught to fear humans, and especially hunters. 

He was no different.

Even as he stepped into that bedroom behind her, even as he saw some grown adult vampires there waiting to try to combat the duo of vampire hunters - his eyes could only linger and remember those terrified eyes of Mydeimos.

Phainon felt nothing as his feet moved faster than his own thoughts after the memory of those golden irises, fast enough to immediately plunge his sword into this fellow vampire hunter’s back - fast enough to cause her to sputter out blood and a gasped wail over the blade in her back so very quickly.

He only immediately ripped it from her back quickly, watching as her body hit the floor with a sickening thud - one that he had heard so many times before as the crimson began to seep and bleed from her body. Dyeing the floor such a bright color of red before she slowed turned her head - obviously, to look at her killer. 

“Why? Why are you killing your own comrades?!” That shrill question ringing out made Phainon tilt his head slightly, studying her as he lazily flexed his wrist with his grip tightening on his sword. 

His eyes only wandered behind his mask, wandering over to the vampires that were terrified, vampires that were watching the both of them.

Vampires.. That would know other vampires..

“Mydeimos.” Was all he uttered in a tired and unremorseful tone, all he bothered to say before leisurely swinging his sword and shoving it into her chest once more harshly - not even blinking over the yell that escaped her lips. Not even caring over the sheer terror that was palpable in the air.

Mydeimos.

That’s all they needed to know. That’s all anyone needed to know - that he was doing it for Mydeimos. Because of Mydeimos. 

His eyes once more trailed over those huddled vampires, those adults and few children that were about to have their lives taken away from them - some now looked.. Confused, looking between each other even. 

Phainon withdrew his sword from her ribcage, only to lash it behind him, humorously splattering blood against the floor as he studied those vampire’s confused and terrified expressions.

That was fine.

Let them spread their rumors, let them get the word out, the vampire hunter that kills other vampire hunters is looking for Mydeimos. 

And only Mydeimos will satisfy him.

──────────────

“Mydei? Are you alright?” Castorice asked as she placed a cup before him, not one he cared to drink out of. But a cup regardless. 

Mydei closed his eyes over it, trying to think of decent words or emotions to feel about all of the rumors and news that had reached his ears over time.

But he couldn’t; “As alright as I can be, given the circumstances..” 

Castorice took her seat at that, a sound Mydei knew very well as the chair scraped against the wood softly; “Why would that.. Vampire hunter guy be after you?”

“Can we even call the guy that? He mainly just kills other hunters, he’s a freak more than anything.” Cipher pointed out with a heavy yawn, leaning back in her chair before flipping a coin.

It always landed on heads, anyway. 

Mydei only gave a sigh, his eyes opening once more to move to the curtained window that was blocking out the moonlight, blocking out the world; “I don’t know.”

He didn’t.

What hunter would be hunting him down so relentlessly? So forcefully and brutally that they wouldn’t even let any other hunter live to accidentally claim their kill?

It sent shivers down his spine to even consider what human he pissed off so badly that they would resort to such violence to their own kind. Usually, the bond between hunters was thicker than blood, they would live and die beside each other in battle to kill vampires.. The idea of one slaughtering their own brethren was.. Eerie to say the least.

“Is there any real proof he’s actually a vampire hunter, or just faking being one?” Castorice asked quietly as she took a seat at their small dining room table with a heavy sigh. One he knew was for his own sake, not hers. 

She was most assuredly fearing for his own sake in this matter.. 

“He shows up at every vampire hunter bounty place that we’ve found information on.. He’s terrifying..” Cipher murmured, even giving a fake little shiver as if to prove her own point as her eyes darted between the other two.

“And he wants to kill Mydei more than anything..” Castorice replied, sounding almost horrified as she even considered such a fate for her longtime friend, “We need to hide him away, we can’t let him be hunted down like this..”

“I’m fine.” Mydei mumbled out as he dropped his eyes to that fancy teacup that had been set before him - blinking at it as he rolled the cup around between his fingers, keenly listening to the gentle clacking of the finery hitting the plate beneath it.

He was fine.

A beat of silence fell upon the trio before Castorice seemed to clear her throat; “Are you sure?”

Mydei tutted at that, pursing his lips for just a moment while he focused wholly on that cup in his hand. 

“I’ll hold my own against him.. Probably. He’s underestimating me.” Mydei grumbled out, because he was quite sure at the least he would be able to put up one hell of a fight.

Sure, a guy murdering his fellow vampire hunters was.. Beyond eerie to consider, but he was still human. And unlike humans, Mydei was a little bit harder to actually keep dead, and just a little bit stronger than most of them.

He was pretty sure he would be able to choke the life from that man extremely easily - just like all the others that had tried to kill him before this one. 

This one was more deranged, and would probably wildly act out, but most of them already did that before dying.

It’s not like that vampire hunter was going to be a special case here. 

“You really have no idea what human you angered so badly that they’re hunting you down for sport?” Cipher asked lazily while leaning back - only making Mydei dart his eyes to her, just for a moment before moving to card a hand through his bangs.

A human he angered..

He really didn’t have many on this list - if anything, he only fought humans when they actively sought him out for such a thing. And even then, he was just acting in self defense with them, wasn’t he?

It's not like he went out of his way to piss any of them off, it just.. His existence did that enough without his input due to his choice in food, anyway. 

“Not a clue.” Mydei grumbled out as he flicked his eyes back to the brown liquid in the cup.

He wasn’t big on coffee - he honestly had no idea how other vampires could handle the stuff, but Castorice was addicted to it and insisted Mydei have some all the time.

“It will help you stop falling asleep everywhere," she had once stated.

But maybe he just liked being able to sit down and fall asleep in three minutes flat, had she ever considered that? He was pretty fond of that, he would even call it a talent of his. 

“Any vampires that might hire a hunter to kill you?” Castorice offered up questioningly, only to move her own cup to her lips and gently take a few sips of it elegantly.

Mydei had to think about the question before leaning back into his chair, pressing out an awfully deep and heavy sigh for a man that didn’t even need air; “Do you know any hunters you could pay to hunt their own kind? Never heard of such a traitor.”

“Whew.. So it really is just someone with a personal vendetta crazy enough to kill their own kind to get to you.. Yeesh.” Cipher murmured abruptly before leaning forward to prop her head up with her hand on the table, blinking at Mydei slowly. 

Castorice hummed as he eyes only blinked at the teacup of coffee in her hand before looking to Mydei, head tilting slightly at her own thoughts; “It’s like.. Weirdly possessive though, isn’t it?”

“Possessive?” Mydei immediately parroted, because what the hell did she mean by that?

Possessive? What about getting hunted down for sport was possessive?

“Like.. The guy won’t even let another hunter kill you so he’s killing them first? Like it has to be by his hands or he won’t be satiated with your death?” Castorice said simply, as if it was just the most obvious thing in the world.

And Mydei found himself choking slightly over it, trying to swallow down the lump that had uncomfortably taken root in his throat before giving a small huff of annoyance.
